A retirement certificate from the Anganwadi Centre
Aadhaar card
Bank account details

scheme_name: Animal Husbandry: Assistance to Small and Marginal Farmers
description: The scheme aims to provide financial assistance to small and marginal farmers for the replacement of productive livestock lost due to notified natural disasters such as floods, landslides, or other calamities.
benefits:
Replacement of Milk, Agricultural, and Transport Animals:

• Milch animals: ₹37,500/- per animal (Buffalo/Cow/Camel/Yak/Mithun) will be payable.- ₹4,000/- per animal (Sheep/Goat/Pig) will be payable.

Agricultural and Haulage Animals: 

• ₹32,000/- per animal (Camel/Horse/Bullock) will be payable.

• ₹20,000/- per animal (Calf/Donkey/Pony/Mule) will be payable.

Poultry Farming:

 - ₹100/- per bird, up to a limit of ₹10,000/- per beneficiary family. The death of birds must be due to a notified natural disaster to be eligible for assistance.
eligibility: 1. The applicant must be a Small or Marginal Farmer from Uttarakhand who has lost their milk, agricultural, or haulage animals due to a notified natural disaster.
application_process:
Mode: Offline. Information about the disaster and the resulting damage is received from various sources. The concerned Patwari verifies the damage and records it in the P-20 form. The Patwari’s report is subsequently verified by the Tehsildar and the Sub-Divisional Magistrate. Approval is then obtained from the District Magistrate. Once the District Magistrate’s approval is received, relief funds are disbursed to the concerned beneficiaries at the Tehsil level.
This assistance shall be limited to the actual loss of productive animals. However, irrespective of the extent of loss, assistance to a single family will be restricted to a maximum of 3 large milch animals, 30 small milch animals, or 3 large agricultural and draught animals (The loss or damage must be verified by a competent authority designated by the State Government).
documents_required:
Form P-20 Entry Confirmation (recorded by the concerned Patwari)
Other supporting documents as required

scheme_name: Appointment of Contract Sports Coaches
description: The scheme facilitates the annual appointment of contract-based sports coaches to conduct various local training camps across Uttarakhand, thereby promoting employment opportunities and strengthening the state’s grassroots sports infrastructure.
benefits: Every year, around 250 coaches benefit from these training camps and gain employment.
eligibility:
1. The applicant must be a sportsperson or a coach from Uttarakhand.
 1. The applicant must be between 21 and 70 years of age.
 1. The applicant must possess the relevant educational and sports qualifications.
 1. The sports coach is not required to be a domicile or permanent resident of Uttarakhand.
application_process:
Mode: Offline. The department organizes local training camps for various sports every year. To ensure the smooth functioning of these camps, sports coaches are appointed on a contractual basis.
At the district level, applications for conducting local training camps are submitted by the District Sports Officers.
Each year, a notification regarding the scheme is published in daily newspapers, usually in the month of March. The training camps are then organized for a maximum duration of 11 months, from 15th April to 15th March.
documents_required: Submission of documents is required in accordance with the department's guidelines to avail the benefits of the scheme.

scheme_name: Aromatic Awareness Programme - Centre for Aromatic Plants
description: The scheme aims to raise awareness about aromatic plants and their benefits, and to provide guidance on cultivation practices suitable to different agricultural climates.
benefits:
• To spread information about aromatic plants and the benefits of their cultivation to the general public.
 - To provide information about crops according to the agricultural climate.
eligibility: 1. Any interested individual who is a resident of Uttarakhand can avail the benefits of the programme.
application_process: Mode: Offline. Any person interested in aromatic plant cultivation can participate in the field-level awareness programmes organized by the Centre for Aromatic Plants (CAP), Selaqui, Dehradun.
documents_required: Documents are required, as per the guidelines of the Centre for Aromatic Plants, Selaqui, Dehradun, to avail the benefits of the programme.

scheme_name: Aromatic Plants Cultivation - Centre for Aromatic Plants
description: The scheme aims to encourage farmers to grow aromatic plants by providing them with free seeds, planting materials, and technical support, helping them increase their income and promote aromatic farming in Uttarakhand.
benefits:
Under this scheme, the following support is provided:

 - Free seeds and planting materials are provided to farmers.
 - Seeds and planting materials for up to 5 Nali (0.1 hectare) per farmer are delivered to the farmer’s nearest motorable road or CAP office.
 - Free technical assistance, consultation, and continuous support are offered to the farmers.
eligibility:
1. The applicant must be a resident of Uttarakhand.
 1. The applicant must be a farmer.
 1. The farmer must either legally own agricultural land or have leased land for a minimum period of 10 years.
 1. The farmer must be interested in aromatic plant cultivation.
application_process:
Mode: Offline. During the awareness program, the farmer will write an application for cultivation addressed to the Director, Aromatic Plant Center, or visit the headquarters in person to submit the application. Land records, Aadhaar card, and mobile number must be attached to the application. After that, CAP's field personnel will conduct a field inspection of the applicant’s land and, after selecting the suitable crop based on the agricultural climate of the area, will submit a recommendation to the Director, CAP. The Director, CAP, will then instruct the District Coordinator of the concerned applicant to provide seeds and planting material.
The District Coordinator prepares a consolidated demand for all farmers in the district and sends it to the Director. Based on the recommendation, quality seeds and planting material are procured for the farmers and delivered to the nearest motorable road to the farmer’s selected land.
documents_required:
Land records documents
Aadhaar card
Mobile number
Other supporting documents as required

scheme_name: Artificial Intelligence
description: The scheme aims to promote awareness, understanding, and practical learning of Artificial Intelligence among school students from classes 9 to 12 and provide them with opportunities to participate in AI coding camps and hands-on experiments.
benefits: UCOST, Regional Science Center, Dehradun, in collaboration with Intel, has established an AI Skills Lab under the AI for Youth program. Students from classes 9 to 12 across the state can participate in AI coding camps and perform hands-on experiments.
eligibility: • The applicant must be a student of class 9 to 12 studying in a government or private school in Uttarakhand.
application_process: Mode: Offline. Schools can register for the AI camp and demonstration sessions. Registration for the AI awareness lectures can be completed by filling out the AI registration form and sending it via email to rscdehradoon@gmail.com and rscdoonai@gmail.com. No additional documents, other than the registration form, are required.
documents_required: No additional documents are required apart from the registration form.

scheme_name: Asian Agri-History Foundation Research Fellowship (M.Sc. Agriculture - All Disciplines)
description: The scheme aims to provide financial support to meritorious students pursuing an M.Sc. in Agriculture across all disciplines by awarding a monthly fellowship of ₹1,200/- for one year.
benefits: Amount of Fellowship: ₹1,200/- per month.
eligibility:
1. The applicant must be a student.
 1. The applicant must be enrolled in an M.Sc. Agriculture program (all disciplines) at Govind Ballabh Pant University of Agriculture and Technology, Pantnagar.
 1. The fellowship is awarded for a duration of one year only.
application_process: Mode: Offline. Students are first invited to submit their applications on the prescribed form. A committee, constituted by the Vice Chancellor, then reviews and evaluates these applications following a defined procedure. Based on the committee’s recommendations, the Vice Chancellor grants approval, after which the students receive their payments.
documents_required: Documents are required in accordance with the university guidelines prescribed for this scheme.

scheme_name: Assistance for Completely Damaged/Destroyed Houses
description: The scheme aims to provide financial assistance to individuals whose residential houses have been completely or partially damaged due to natural disasters in Uttarakhand. Under this scheme, compensation is provided to disaster-affected families to support them in rebuilding or repairing their homes.
benefits:
Under this scheme, the following assistance is provided:

 - Pucca house, Kutcha house, severely damaged/destroyed house, or partially damaged/destroyed house: ₹1,20,000/- per house in plain areas.
 - For hilly areas (including districts covered under the Integrated Action Plan): ₹1,30,000/- per house.
 - Pucca house (other than hut) with at least 15% damage: ₹6,500/- per house.
 - Kutcha house (other than hut) with at least 15% damage: ₹4,000/- per house.
 - Damaged/destroyed hut: ₹8,000/- per hut. (A “hut” means a temporary, transferable, and below-grade unit constructed with materials such as thatch, mud, or plastic, and is traditionally recognised as a hut by the State/District Administration.) Note: The damaged house must be verified as an authorised construction by the competent authority of the State Government.

• Cattle shed attached to the house: ₹3,000/- per cattle shed.
eligibility:
1. The applicant must be a resident of Uttarakhand.
1. The applicant must be the owner of a disaster-affected house.
application_process: Mode: Offline. Information about the disaster and the resulting damage is received from various sources. The concerned Patwari verifies the damage and records it in the P-20 form. The Patwari’s report is subsequently verified by the Tehsildar and the Sub-Divisional Magistrate. Approval is then obtained from the District Magistrate. Once the District Magistrate’s approval is received, relief funds are disbursed to the concerned beneficiaries at the Tehsil level.
documents_required:
Form P-20 Entry Confirmation (recorded by the concerned Patwari)
Other supporting documents as required

scheme_name: Assistance for Damage to Agricultural Land and Other Losses
description: The scheme aims to provide financial relief to farmers whose agricultural land has been damaged due to natural disasters such as floods, landslides, avalanches, or river diversions. Under this scheme, a minimum of ₹5,000/- and a maximum of ₹47,000/- is provided to the beneficiaries.
benefits:
• Under this scheme, in cases where farmers with agricultural land up to 2 hectares suffer damage and the layer of sand or sediment exceeds 3 inches, financial assistance is provided at the rate of ₹18,000/- per hectare for the removal of debris, leveling of land, or repair and restoration of fisheries reservoirs in hilly areas. A minimum of ₹2,200/- is payable to each beneficiary under this relief.
 - Farmers are provided ₹47,000/- per hectare for land damaged due to landslides, avalanches, or river diversions, with a minimum assistance of ₹5,000/- payable to each beneficiary.
eligibility:
1. The applicant must be a resident of Uttarakhand.
1. The applicant must be a farmer/family who has suffered disaster-related losses.
1. The beneficiary must not be receiving or have received benefits for the same loss under any other scheme.
1. The applicant must have suffered damage to land that they legally own, according to revenue records.
application_process: Mode: Offline. Information about the disaster and the resulting damage is received from various sources. The concerned Patwari verifies the damage and records it in the P-20 form. The Patwari’s report is subsequently verified by the Tehsildar and the Sub-Divisional Magistrate. Approval is then obtained from the District Magistrate. Once the District Magistrate’s approval is received, relief funds are disbursed to the concerned beneficiaries at the Tehsil level.
documents_required:
Form P-20 Entry Confirmation (recorded by the concerned Patwari)
Other supporting documents as required

scheme_name: Assistance for Purchase of Traditional Musical Instruments and Costumes for Scheduled Caste/Tribe Individuals
description: The scheme aims to support scheduled caste and scheduled tribe individuals whose livelihood depends on traditional arts by providing them with essential musical instruments and costumes.
benefits:
• Persons belonging to the Scheduled Castes or Scheduled Tribes, whose source of income is through their traditional art, and who do not possess musical instruments or costumes, are provided with traditional musical instruments (such as Dhol, Damaun, Masakbeen, Ransingha, Trumpet, Nagada, Shield, Sword, etc.) and costumes free of cost to help them sustain their livelihood.
 - The instruments are provided only once in a lifetime.
eligibility:
1. The applicant must be a resident of Uttarakhand.
1. The applicant must be a folk artist.
1. The applicant must belong to the Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe community.
1. The applicant's monthly income must not exceed ₹2,000/-.
1. Only one set of musical instruments is provided per artist in a family under this scheme.
application_process:
Mode: Offline. The Directorate of Culture publishes an advertisement for providing traditional musical instruments and costumes to eligible SC/ST individuals. 
Following the advertisement, the concerned individuals are required to submit to the Director of the Culture Directorate a certificate of monthly income of ₹2,000/- issued by the Tehsildar, a certificate of artist/instrument, Aadhaar card, caste certificate, bank account details including account number and IFSC code, PAN card, permanent residence certificate, and an affidavit stating that the beneficiary has not received any grant under other schemes.
Eligible beneficiaries are selected by a committee constituted under the chairmanship of the Secretary of Culture at the Directorate level. After the selection process, beneficiaries can collect the musical instruments from the Directorate.
documents_required:
Certificate of monthly income of ₹2,000/- issued by the Tehsildar
Certificate of artist/instrument
Aadhaar card
Caste certificate
Bank account details including account number and IFSC code
PAN card
Permanent residence certificate
Affidavit stating that the beneficiary has not received any grant under other schemes

scheme_name: Assistance Scheme for Handloom Spinning-Weaving Women Workers
description: The scheme aims to provide financial support to traditional women workers whose primary occupation is handloom weaving, spinning, or related weaving activities. Under this scheme, eligible women workers are provided with handloom equipment, including looms & related equipment, worth upto ₹25,000/-.
benefits: Under this scheme, for providing handloom / pantloom / frameloom and other related tools and equipment to selected women workers, 90% of the total cost (up to a maximum of ₹25,000/-) will be borne by the department, while the remaining 10% will be contributed by the beneficiary herself.
eligibility:
1. The applicant must be a resident of Uttarakhand.
 1. The applicant must be a woman worker who belong to a family whose ancestral occupation is weaving, spinning, knitting, or allied handloom activities.
 1. Preference will be given to women workers who have experience in the handloom sector but are unable to carry out weaving work due to the unavailability of a loom.
 1. The woman worker must be registered with the Government of India or Government of Uttarakhand.
application_process:
Mode: Online. Application forms can be obtained from the General Manager, District Industries Centre, or downloaded from the departmental website at https://doi.uk.org.
Along with the application form, applicants must submit a copy of their Aadhaar card, bank account details, relevant registration certificate (if registered with the Government of India or the State Government), and other documents, photographs, or certificates related to handicrafts or weaving. These documents should be submitted through the General Manager of the concerned District Industries Centre.
Selection Process:
A committee constituted under the chairmanship of the General Manager, District Industries Centre, will select eligible women workers at the district level as per the prescribed criteria. The list of selected beneficiaries along with the necessary details will be forwarded to the Directorate of Industries for approval. After approval, 90% of the sanctioned amount will be transferred directly to the bank accounts of the selected women workers.
documents_required:
Copy of Aadhaar Card
Bank account details (passbook or statement)
Relevant registration certificate (if registered with the Government of India or the State Government)
Documents or certificates related to handicrafts/weaving work
Recent passport-size photographs
Any other supporting documents as required by the department

scheme_name: Assistance to Handloom Artisans - Uttarakhand
description: The scheme aims to provide financial support to disaster-affected handloom artisans for the repair or repurchase of damaged tools, equipment, raw materials, and finished products.
benefits:
Under this scheme, the following assistance is provided to disaster-affected artisans:

• For the repurchase of damaged tools and equipment: ₹ 5,000/- per artisan for the repurchase of tools. - For damage to raw materials or products under production or finished: ₹ 5,000/- per artisan for raw materials.
eligibility:
1. The applicant must be a resident of Uttarakhand.
1. The applicant must be a disaster-affected artisan.
application_process:

Once the District Magistrate’s approval is received, relief funds are disbursed to the concerned beneficiaries at the Tehsil level.
It is necessary to have the damage and its replacement duly verified by the competent authority appointed by the State Government.

Other supporting documents as required

scheme_name: Atal Awas Yojana - Uttarakhand
description: Under this scheme, financial assistance of ₹1,30,000/- is provided for constructing houses in hilly areas and ₹1,20,000/- for plain areas to homeless Scheduled Caste families who are below the poverty line (BPL) or fall within a defined income limit.
benefits:
Financial Assistance

• ₹1,30,000/- for hilly areas
• ₹1,20,000/- for plain areas

> Note: The amount is disbursed in 3 installments to construct a house.
eligibility:
1. The applicant should be a native of Uttarakhand.
1. The applicant should belong to a Scheduled Caste family.
1. The applicant should belong to the Below Poverty Line (BPL) category or have an annual income not exceeding ₹48,000/-.
1. The applicant should not have their own house.
1. The applicant should have their own land for constructing a house.
application_process:
Mode: Offline. Every year, targets are assigned to the districts. The districts allocate targets to the development blocks on the basis of population. Applications are received at the development block level.
It is mandatory to attach the caste certificate, income certificate, photograph, Aadhaar card, CBS Aadhaar-seeded/linked bank account details, and property documents with the application.
The application forms are verified by the Village Development Officer/Gram Panchayat Development Officer, after which a priority list is prepared at the block development level. From the applications received, eligible beneficiaries are selected by a committee comprising the Chief Development Officer, Block Development Officer, and District Social Welfare Officer. Thereafter, the District Social Welfare Officer initiates the process of fund allocation as per the committee’s recommendations.
documents_required:
Passport-size Photograph
Caste Certificate
Income Certificate
Aadhaar Card
CBS-Linked Bank Passbook Copy
Land Ownership Documents
Any other documents as required

Uttarakhand govt. invites Atal Ayushman Uttarakhand Yojana Online Registration Form at ayushmanuttarakhand.org. Ayushman Bharat – PM Jan Arogya Yojana (AB-PMJAY scheme) was launched by PM Modi on 23 September 2018 which provides facility of free treatment upto Rs. 5 lakh to around 5 lakh poor families of Uttarakhand. Now the state govt. has taken this initiative forward and launched Atal Ayushman Uttarakhand Yojana (AAUY) for which online registration forms are invited at the official website. 

AAUY Scheme would add around 18 lakh families in this PM-JAY scheme. Now the total Ayushman Bharat beneficiaries in Uttarakhand would be 23 lakh households who can avail free treatment at any govt. / private empanelled hospitals. The state govt. provides health insurance cover upto Rs. 5 lakh per family per year for secondary and tertiary care. There is no restriction on family size, age or gender and hospitalization process has been made cashless and paperless.

Latest Update – The online application process for registration & preparation of Atal Ayushman Uttarakhand Yojana Golden Cards has now been changed. The new application process is offline and its complete description is mentioned at the official website ayushmanuttarakhand.org. Please check the complete details on how to apply for AAUY and get your golden card prepared.

In Atal Ayushman Uttarakhand Yojana, no pre-existing condition has been excluded. Till date, there are more than 171 hospitals empanelled (101 government & 74 private) under Atal Ayushman Uttarakhand Yojana (AAUY).

Atal Ayushman Uttarakhand Yojana (AAUY) Online Registration 2020

Uttarakhand has become the first state in the country which provides cashless treatment to all its citizens. The complete procedure to apply online for Atal Ayushman Uttarakhand Yojana has been specified as follows:-

Visit the official website ayushmanuttarakhand.org

At the homepage, click at the “Online Registration” link or directly click this link

Afterwards, the Atal Ayushman Bharat Yojana online registration form will appear as follows:-

Atal Ayushman Uttarakhand Yojana Online Registration Form

Here candidates needs to enter their personal details including address, voter card number, ration card number, e-mail ID & mobile phone number and details of their family members.

Finally, candidates can click at the “Submit” button to complete the registration process.

Atal Ayushman Uttarakhand Yojana Golden Card

For any technical queries, candidates can contact at the integrated Ayushman Bharat Yojana helpline number at 104 / 14555.

https://ayushmanuttarakhand.org/search

The family search page to find name in AAUY Scheme will appear as shown below:-

If you’re searching with Mobile No. or Name, District Selection is Mandatory. If you’re searching with NFSA (Ration Card), Voter ID 2012, MSBY Card No. District Selection is not Mandatory.

All the beneficiaries can now download the AAUY mobile app through the link given below:-

Ayushman Bharat Scheme in Uttarakhand – Scheme Highlights

Below are the essential features and highlights of AAUY scheme:-

Health insurance cover of Rs. 5 Lakhs per family per year for secondary and tertiary care.

There is no restriction on family size, age or gender under AAUY Scheme.

All members of eligible families as present in SECC 2011 data are automatically covered under this Ayushman Bharat Yojana in Uttarakhand.

In case of hospitalization, poor people need not pay any money as this treatment is absolutely free.

All the pre-existing conditions are covered from 1st day of the policy under PM Jan Arogya Yojana. The benefit cover will include pre & post hospitalization expenses.

People can go to any public / empanelled private hospitals across the country and can avail treatment benefits under AAUY. For this treatment, beneficiaries needs to carry any prescribed ID to receive treatment at the hospital.

scheme_name: Atithi Uttarakhand Home-Stay Registration
description: The scheme aims to promote rural tourism and generate local employment by enabling residents to register their homes as certified home-stays that offer safe, affordable accommodation and meal facilities to tourists in Uttarakhand.
benefits:
Under this scheme, any house owner in the state who wishes to make the residential rooms of their house available to tourists can register their home with the Tourism Department as a home-stay. After registration, the owner can provide night stay and meals to guests and charge a fee for these services. The main objective of this scheme is to offer accommodation and food facilities to tourists and to provide employment opportunities to rural residents at their homes. 
After registration, the respective accommodation is listed on the department’s website under the Home Stay directory, allowing any tourist to obtain information from the website and avail night stay facilities.
eligibility:
1. For registration under this scheme, a No Objection Certificate (NOC) must be issued by the Development Authority/Local Body in urban areas, and by the Gram Pradhan in rural areas. 
 1. The accommodation unit must be entirely residential, and the house owner must reside there with their family.
 1. There must be at least one and a maximum of six rooms available for guests/tourists.
 1. The residential unit must have a toilet, should be clean and well-maintained, equipped with fire safety equipment, and built in a structurally robust manner.
application_process:
Mode: Online. Registration for Atithi Uttarakhand Home-Stay has to be done online at https://uttarakhandtourism.gov.in> Trade > Homestay Registration, for which Aadhaar number and the Aadhaar-linked mobile number are mandatory, and during the registration process, the applicant must attach the affidavit mentioned in the application form, PAN card, a copy of the approved building map (plan), photographs of the home-stay (including the home-stay name, room interiors, toilet, and kitchen), a copy of land ownership documents (Khata, Khatauni/Registry papers), the old registration certificate of the Paying Guest House (in case of an old unit), the registration fee - ₹500 through NEFT/online/offline, the character certificate issued by the district administration, and the Fire Department NOC/fire extinguisher bill (as specified by the District Tourism Development Officer). 
Thereafter, an inspection is carried out by departmental officers and the registration number is provided to the applicant; Once registered, the owner can offer night stay facilities to guests/tourists by charging the prescribed fee.
documents_required:
Affidavit as mentioned in the application form
PAN card
Copy of approved building map (plan)
Photographs of the home stay (including name board, room interiors, toilet, and kitchen)
Land ownership documents (Khata, Khatauni / Registry papers)
Previous Paying Guest House registration certificate (if applicable)
Registration fee of ₹500/- (NEFT/online/offline)
Character certificate issued by the District Administration
Fire Department NOC / Fire Extinguisher bill (as prescribed by the District Tourism Development Officer)
Other supporting documents as required

scheme_name: Award of Merit Scholarship for Agricultural Engineering Students (B.Tech 3rd/4th Year)
description: The scheme aims to support meritorious students pursuing B.Tech in Agricultural Engineering in their 3rd and 4th years by providing scholarship of ₹2000/- per month for one year.
benefits: Rate of Scholarship: ₹2,000/- per month.
eligibility:
1. The applicant must be a student.
 1. The applicant must be enrolled in the 3rd or 4th year of the B.Tech (Agricultural Engineering) course at Govind Ballabh Pant University of Agriculture and Technology, Pantnagar.
 1. The scholarship is awarded for a duration of one year only.
application_process: Mode: Offline. Students are first invited to submit their applications on the prescribed form. A committee, constituted by the Vice Chancellor, then reviews and evaluates these applications following a defined procedure. Based on the committee’s recommendations, the Vice Chancellor grants approval, after which the students receive their payments.
documents_required: Documents are required in accordance with the university guidelines prescribed for this scheme.

scheme_name: Award Scheme for Candidates Selected in NDA, IMA, OTA, INA, IAF
description: Under this scheme, a one-time award of ₹50,000/- is given to each candidate from Uttarakhand who has been selected for service at premier defence academies such as the NDA, IMA, OTA, INA, and IAF.
benefits: Award Amount: ₹50,000/- per candidate
eligibility:
1. The candidate must be a native or permanent resident of Uttarakhand.
 1. The candidate should have been selected for service at one of the premier defence academies, such as National Defence Academy (NDA), Indian Military Academy (IMA), Officers Training Academy (OTA), Indian Naval Academy (INA) or Indian Air Force (IAF).
 1. The applicant must either be currently undergoing training at the respective academy or have been formally inducted into the defence service.
 1. The candidate must have successfully completed the relevant training and course.
application_process:
Mode: Offline. Candidates must apply after being selected for the service and completing their training. They should download the application form from the Department of Higher Education’s website at https://he.uk.gov.in/ and attach the following documents: the candidate’s Aadhaar card, PAN card, bank account details, permanent residence certificate, appointment letter, training certificate, proof of joining after training (if applicable), and a declaration stating that they have not previously availed the benefit of this scheme.
The completed application form, along with the attached documents, must be submitted to the Directorate of Higher Education, Haldwani. After preliminary scrutiny of applications at the Directorate level, an amount of ₹50,000 is released from the government every six months.
documents_required:
Aadhaar card
PAN card
Bank account details
Permanent residence certificate
Appointment letter
Training certificate
Proof of joining, if applicable, after completion of training
A declaration stating that they have not previously availed the benefit of this scheme

scheme_name: Award Scheme to Encourage Entrepreneurs - Uttarakhand
description: The scheme aims to recognize exceptional craftsmanship among registered artisans and weavers in Uttarakhand by encouraging innovation, creativity, and excellence in the handicrafts and handloom sectors through state and district-level awards.
benefits:
*Nature of the Award:*
*1. State Level Award*
For the best artisans in the handicraft sector:

 - First Prize: ₹15,000/-
 - Second Prize: ₹10,000/-
 - Third Prize: ₹7,000/-

*For the best weavers in the handloom (cotton and woolen) sector:*

 - First Prize: ₹15,000/-
 - Second Prize: ₹10,000/-
 - Third Prize: ₹7,000/-

*2. District Level Award*
For the best artisans in the handicraft sector:

 - First Prize: ₹6,000/-
 - Second Prize: ₹4,000/-

*For the best weavers in the handloom (cotton and woolen) sector:*

 - First Prize: ₹6,000/-
 - Second Prize: ₹4,000/-
eligibility:
1. The applicant must be a registered artisan or weaver, or an industry registered as Handloom Weaver/Handicraftsman under the Directorate of Industries, Uttarakhand, or the Development Commissioner (Handicrafts/Handloom), Government of India.
 1. The applicant must be an individual artisan or weaver belonging to a registered handicraft or handloom cooperative society, or a registered non-governmental organization (NGO) within the state of Uttarakhand to be eligible for the award.
 1. The artisan’s/weaver’s cooperative society or institution must not be a loan defaulter with any department or bank.
 1. An artisan/weaver who has already received an award cannot apply again for the next three consecutive years.
application_process:
Mode: Online. Application forms can be obtained from the office of the General Manager, District Industries Centre (DIC) or downloaded from the departmental website at https://doi.uk.org.
The duly filled application form, along with a copy of the Aadhaar card, relevant handicraft/weaving-related documents, photographs, and certificates, must be submitted through the General Manager, District Industries Centre of the concerned district by the due date.
The three copy of application form must be submitted, along with a demand draft of ₹50/- payable in favour of the General Manager, District Industries Centre.
Selection Process:
For the District Level Awards, selections are made by a District Level Selection Committee constituted under the chairmanship of the District Magistrate/Chief Development Officer.
For the State Level Awards, selections are made by a State Level Selection Committee constituted under the chairmanship of the Director of Industries, Uttarakhand.
documents_required:
Copy of Aadhaar Card
Handicraft/Weaving-related documents (proof of work, registration, etc.)
Photographs of the products or work samples
Relevant certificates or recognitions, if any
Demand Draft of ₹50/- payable in favour of the General Manager, District Industries Centre

scheme_name: AYUSH Health and Wellness Centre - Ayushman Bharat Yojana
description: The scheme aims to provide accessible, affordable, and holistic healthcare services based on Ayurveda, Yoga, Unani and Homeopathy systems to people of all age groups.
benefits:
A total of 300 AYUSH Health and Wellness Centres are operating in the state. At these centres, medicines are distributed according to the specific disease, and yoga and naturopathy treatments are provided as per the condition.

 - Counselling based on nature testing and seasonal routines- screening and diagnosis of non-communicable diseases such as diabetes, hypertension, oral cancer, breast cancer, and cervical cancer, are conducted.
 - Medicinal plants are also distributed.
 - OPD charges have been fixed at ₹1.00 per person in rural areas and ₹2.00 per person in urban areas.
eligibility:
• The beneficiary must be a resident of Uttarakhand.
• The beneficiary may belong to any age group.
• The beneficiary must be registered at a government-recognized Ayurvedic, Unani, or Homeopathic dispensary or hospital.
application_process: Mode: Offline. The beneficiary needs to register at a government-recognized Ayurvedic, Unani, or Homeopathic dispensary or hospital.
documents_required:
Registration Proof at the Government Ayurvedic/Unani/Homeopathic Dispensary or Hospital
Identity Proof
Any other document as required

scheme_name: Bakri Palan Yojana
description: The scheme aims to promote goat rearing as a source of self-employment and livelihood generation for eligible beneficiaries, particularly from SECC categories, by providing financial support for rearing a goat unit.
benefits:
• Self-employment in goat rearing is facilitated by providing beneficiaries with a goat unit comprising 10 female goats and 1 male goat for a period of 10 to 14 months. 
 - The total cost of the unit is ₹70,000/-, of which 90% (₹63,000/-) is funded by the State Government, and the remaining 10% (₹7,000/-) is contributed by the beneficiary.
eligibility:
1. The applicant must be a resident of Uttarakhand.
1. The applicant must belong to the General, Scheduled Caste, or Scheduled Tribe category.
1. The applicant must be included in the SECC (Socio-Economic and Caste Census) category.
1. The applicant should have an interest in goat rearing.
application_process:
Mode: Offline. Interested beneficiaries must submit their proposal in an open meeting of the Gram Sabha. Once the proposal is approved, the beneficiary shall submit it to the Veterinary Officer, Livestock Extension Officer, or Gram Panchayat Development Officer of the respective area, or the Gram Panchayat may submit it on behalf of the beneficiary.
Based on the recommendation of the village-level selection committee, the final selection is made by the development block-level committee and forwarded to the Animal Husbandry Department. After selection, the beneficiary will receive funds for purchasing goats through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) within one to two months.
Applicants must submit Aadhaar card, bank account details, and caste certificate along with their proposal.
documents_required:
Aadhaar Card
Bank Account details
Caste Certificate
Other supporting documents as required

scheme_name: Bal Swasthya Karyakram - Uttarakhand
description: This initiative aims to ensure the survival, healthy growth, and overall well-being of children aged 0–5 years by providing accessible, comprehensive and quality healthcare services.
department: Medical Health And Family Welfare Department
benefits: Under this Programme, medical services are provided to children aged 0–5 years through Special Newborn Care Units (SNCUs), Newborn Stabilization Units (NBSUs), and Nutritional Rehabilitation Centres (NRCs). Additionally, ASHA workers, Anganwadi workers, and ANMs distribute Vitamin A and IFA syrup free of cost to children aged 0–5 years.
eligibility: 1. The beneficiary must be a child between 0 and 5 years of age from Uttarakhand.
application_process: Mode: Offline. SNCU, NBSU, and NBCC are operational in the district hospitals, sub-district hospitals, primary health centers, and community health centers across the state. Services can be availed by registering at these centers.
documents_required:
1. Birth certificate
2. Other documents as required

scheme_name: Basic Kayaking Course
description: The scheme aims to train and certify youth of Uttarakhand as skilled kayaking instructors with essential life-saving skills. Under this scheme, specialized training in life-saving techniques and kayaking is provided to selected youth beneficiaries of Uttarakhand.
benefits: The beneficiary will receive the training in basic kayaking.
eligibility:
1. The applicant must be a youth of Uttarakhand.
1. The applicant must be at least 18 years of age.
1. The applicant should be able to swim 100 meters within 3 minutes.
1. The applicant must be educated.
1. The applicant must be mentally and physically fit.
1. The applicant must have prior training in life-saving techniques and water sports operations from a recognized institute.

> The total number of 15 beneficiaries will be selected.
application_process:
Mode: Offline. The prescribed application form must be duly filled and submitted along with the required documents to the office of the District Tourism Development Officer.
The applications are evaluated on practical parameters by the trainers from the National Institute of Water Sports (NIWS), Goa.
documents_required: Applicants are required to submit the necessary documents in accordance with the guidelines specified by the department.

scheme_name: Bee Keeping
description: The scheme aims to promote beekeeping as a sustainable livelihood by providing subsidized bee boxes, bee colonies, and training support to farmers, thereby increasing honey production, enhancing farm income, and strengthening the beekeeping sector in Uttarakhand.
benefits:
Under this scheme:

 - Bee families (bees, including the queen bee) and bee colonies (bee boxes) are provided with a 40% subsidy (maximum cost per bee box is ₹2,000/- and per bee colony is ₹2,000/-). 50 bee boxes are provided in plain areas and 25 in hilly areas.
 - For example, if a bee box and bee colony cost ₹200/-, the farmer has to deposit ₹120/- at the concerned Horticulture Mobile team Centre. The government bears a subsidy of ₹80/-, and the farmer receives the box for ₹120/-.
 - If a farmer wishes to keep bee colonies in their own orchards, financial assistance of ₹350/- per bee colony is provided.
 - If a farmer wants to receive training, the department provides a free seven-day beekeeping training program. Along with the training, the farmer is given ₹100/- per day (totaling ₹700/-) and ₹50/- per day (totaling ₹350/-). A total of ₹1,050/- is provided to each beneficiary.
eligibility:
1. The applicant must be a resident of Uttarakhand.
 1. The applicant must be a farmer interested in beekeeping.
application_process:
Mode: Offline. The concerned farmer must submit an application for bee boxes and bee colonies at the respective Horticulture Mobile team Centre and attach their address, mobile number, Aadhaar card, residence certificate, and bank account details. After submission, the Horticulture Mobile team Centre forwards the application to the district office or the Jeolikote Centre. If the application is approved, the farmer is informed over the phone, and an acceptance letter is also issued.
The farmer can then collect the bee boxes and bee colonies from the Jeolikote Centre or the district office at a 40% subsidy. Beneficiary selection is made on a first-come, first-served basis and depends on budget availability.
For training, farmers must submit a separate training application at their Horticulture Mobile team Centre, along with their address, mobile number, Aadhaar card, residence certificate, and bank account details. The application is forwarded to the district office. When 10-30 farmers in a district express interest in beekeeping, a group is formed, and the department schedules the training date and informs the farmers by phone. On the scheduled date, farmers must attend the training. After completing the training, each farmer receives ₹1,050/-, either in cash or through a bank transfer.
documents_required:
Aadhaar card
Address proof
Mobile number
Residence certificate
Bank account details
Other supporting documents as required

scheme_name: Bhesaj Krishi Vikas Yojana (Herbal Cultivation Programme)
description: The scheme aims to promote the cultivation of medicinal and herbal plants (Jadi-Buti) among local farmers and unemployed youth, providing sustainable employment and improving their economic well-being.
benefits:
*From the cultivation of medicinal plants, the following estimated profits can be earned:*

• Kuth species: ₹1,000/- per nali per year- Kutki species: ₹660/- per nali per year- Big Cardamom species: ₹1,120/- per nali per year (from the fourth year onwards)- Sarpagandha species: ₹1,200/- per nali per year- Tejpata species: ₹1,200/- per nali per year (after ten years)
*This cultivation provides additional employment to farmers and strengthens their economic condition.*
eligibility:
1. The applicant must be a resident of Uttarakhand.
 1. The applicant must be unemployed.
 1. The applicant must have at least five Nali of land available.
 1. The applicant must have an Aadhaar card.
 1. The applicant must be interested in obtaining employment opportunities through herbal cultivation.
application_process:
Mode: Offline. The District Bhesaj Coordinator, Bhesaj Vikas Ikai, selects residents of designated villages/pattis within the chosen development block who are willing to work in a cluster (10 farmers from 2–3 villages) and wish to cultivate herbs suitable to the local climate and altitude through a training camp. The cluster-wise list of selected participants is sent to headquarters for the demand of saplings as per the action plan. Subsequently, these individuals are ensured to receive saplings from selected nurseries in July–August (rainy season) according to the five-nali standard.
The District Bhesaj Coordinator then registers the planted saplings with the Herbal Research and Development Institute, Gopeshwar. Three months before harvest, the District Bhesaj Coordinator issues a free challan to any market or pharmacy selling the cultivated species.
documents_required:
Aadhaar Card
Other documents as required

scheme_name: Bicycle/Sewing Machine Assistance Scheme (UKBOCWWB)
description: Under the scheme, bicycles are provided to registered building & construction workers in plain areas, while sewing machines are provided to registered workers or their dependents in mountainous/hilly areas. These benefits are granted only once in a lifetime.
benefits: Bicycles are provided to construction workers in the plain areas, while sewing machines are provided to construction workers or their dependents in the hilly areas.

The online application is made through Shramik Suvidha Kendras. 
A self-attested photocopy of the Shramik Card, Aadhaar Card, and a self-declaration certificate must be submitted along with the application form.
After verification through the departmental investigation, bicycles/sewing machines are provided to the construction workers by the department. 
This benefit is given only once in a lifetime.

Labour Card
Aadhaar Card
Self-declaration certificate

If you are looking to check your name in the BPL list upto 2020-2021 to avail benefits of social welfare schemes such as Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (Gramin), PM Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY), PM Sahaj Bijli Har Ghar Yojana (Saubhagya) or any other, you are at the right place. The selection of beneficiaries for may social welfare schemes is done on the basis of BPL households in the state/country.

The inclusion or exclusion of a family in the BPL list is already decided in the Socio-Economic Caste Census-2011 data and the complete state wise list of BPL households can be downloaded from the respective websites of state departments. The BPL list is is must for those who are looking to enroll themselves for availing the benefits of welfare schemes in 2019-2020, especially designed for the BPL families.

The complete state wise list of BPL families / households / candidates can be seen at the official websites of state government departments or in SECC-2011 data. Other than the BPL list, government may decide few other parameters for the selection of beneficiaries for various schemes. It is important to note that there is no proper BPL List 2020-21 which is publicly available, as the list is a part of Socio-Economic Cast Census Data – 2011.

BPL List (Till 2020-2021) Based on (SECC-2011) NREGA Data

People can check their name in the BPL list through any of the 2 methods described below:-

1. Based On Inclusion & Exclusion in NREGA Scheme

In Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA Scheme), under this scheme most of the BPL households are covered / included, hence, you one can check name in BPL list by looking at the list of NREGA job cards at its official website. For checking name in the all India final BPL list, based on NREGA job cards list, below is the complete procedure:-

STEP 1: To download the BPL List from SECC 2011 Data (based on MGNREGA data), candidates can directly click this link – https://nrega.nic.in/.

All India BPL List Based on NREGA

STEP 2: To check your name in the IPPE2 final BPL list, candidates can click the “State Name” to reach to the next page which will be displayed as below. 

Find Name in NREGA BPL List

STEP 3: On this screen, users have to select the financial year (Up to 2020-2021), district, block, panchayat and then click on the “Proceed” button which will take you to the list of NREGA job cards (Almost all of those belongs to the BPL families).

On the next page, you will see the complete list of all NREGA Job Cards or the most of the BPL candidates as shown below.

BPL List Based on NREGA

STEP 5: Finally, candidates can click the “Job Card Number / जॉब कार्ड संख्या” to check the complete details of that particular candidate.

However, there is no option to download this IPPE2 SECC list / BPL list file in MS Excel or PDF format. Moreover, candidates can print it also using “Print” command in Windows (ctrl+P). If any person belonging to BPL category is able to find their name in the downloaded SECC 2011 data list (All India Final BPL List 2020-2021), then person would be eligible to avail benefits of various govt. schemes.

Candidates can can press ctrl+F buttons to open the find dialog and search their name in the BPL list based on NREGA upto 2020-2021. If there are multiple entries with the same name, then match it with the address, name of parents and other details.

MGNREGA Convergent Planning List

All the people can also check their name in the MGNREGA convergent planning list. This list is prepared by the central govt. after inclusion of National Rural livelihood Mission (NRLM), Indira Awas Yojana (IAY), Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-GKY) and National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP) beneficiaries. The MGNREGA Convergent Planning list can be accessed through the link:-

http://mnregaweb4.nic.in/The MGNREGA Convergent Planning List will appear as shown below:-

MGNREGA Convergent Planning List SECC 2011 Data

Here candidates can select the State, District, Tehsil / Taluk, Gram Panchayat and click at “Submit” button to open the MGNREGA Convergent Planning Households List as shown below:-

MGNREGA Convergent Planning Households List

This list would contain the SECC TIN Number, district, tehsil / taluk, block, gram panchayat, village name, household size, age, gender, social category and job card details.

SECC-2011 Data Summary – Deprivation Households Data

People can check SECC 2011 Data Summary at the official website – secc.gov.in and the entire summary report can be checked at the link below:-http://secc.gov.in/statewiseSeccDataSummaryReport?reportType=SECC%20Data%20Summary#

Click at the option of “Save Report” to save the entire SECC-2011 data report in “Microsoft Office Excel Worksheet” file. Candidates can even check the zone wise list which comprises of the type of households, gender, disability, education, caste, income and employment profile along with assets and land ownership. In addition, category wise list is available for SC / ST / Female / Disabled and other category people. All the displayed data is on the basis of income source, salaried jobs, house type, exclusion, inclusion and deprivation.

The total number of households belonging to Below Poverty Line (BPL) which is an economic benchmark in India stands at about 107.4 million (10.74 crore) in 2011 as per the official data.

Candidates can also check SECC Family Member Details to get Socio Economic Caste Census (SECC) family member details.

scheme_name: Cancer Day Care Centre - Uttarakhand
description: The scheme aims to ensure early detection & timely treatment of cancer by providing accessible & affordable healthcare services within the state. scheme_name: Cash Prize to Players and their Coaches for Winning Medals in National and International Competitions
description: The scheme aims to recognize and honor players and their coaches from the state who have achieved remarkable success and won medals at the national and international level in the field of sports. There is a provision to award prize money ranging from a minimum of ₹10,000/- to a maximum of ₹2 crore.
benefits:
• Under this scheme, athletes who achieve significant success at the national and international levels, along with their coaches, are awarded cash prizes. 
 - There is a provision to award prize money ranging from a minimum of ₹10,000/- to a maximum of ₹2 crore. - Detailed information about the awards is available on the department's website: [https://sports.uk.gov.in](https://sports.uk.gov.in/).
eligibility: 1. Players and their coaches from Uttarakhand who have achieved remarkable success at the national and international levels in the field of sports are eligible.
application_process:
Mode: Offline. Offline applications are invited twice a year by the Sports Directorate. Applications are accepted in the month of January for prize distribution of games held from 01 January to 30 June, and again in July for prize distribution of games held from 01 July to 31 December.
The application form can be downloaded from the department’s website. The form must be accompanied by the following documents: the athlete’s Aadhaar card, bank account number, passport-size photograph, details of the medal won at the competition along with complete certificates, permanent residence certificate of Uttarakhand, and the coach’s qualification documents (either a one-year sports diploma or an equivalent certificate, or a six-week training certificate issued by the National Federation of the concerned sport). In addition, a declaration on a ₹10/- stamp paper must be provided, certifying that the player has been regularly trained by the coach for at least 180 days during the one year preceding the medal achievement. The coach’s Aadhaar card and bank account details must also be submitted.
It is mandatory for medal-winning players of the National School Games to get their sports certificates verified by the School Education Department; for winners of World/All India University Competitions or Championships by the Higher Education Department/University; for winners of Khelo India, Indian Rural Sports Competitions, or National Women’s Sports Festivals by the Youth Welfare Department; and for winners of All India Police Sports Competitions or World Police/Fire Games by the Uttarakhand Police Department. After verification, the application form must be submitted to the Sports Directorate within the stipulated period along with the recommendation of the concerned department, institution, or recognized State Sports Association.
Once the documents are examined and verified by the Sports Directorate, the prize money is released to both the player and the coach.

Document for Players:
Aadhaar card of the Player
Bank Account details
Passport-size Photo
Complete Details and Certificate of the Competition in which the medal has been won 
Permanent Residence Certificate of Uttarakhand

One year sports diploma of the coach or equivalent or 06 weeks certificate 
Certificate of training of the National Association of the concerned sport 
Details related to the training of the coach on a stamp paper of ₹ 10 / - (by which the player has been regularly trained for at least 180 days or more a year before the medal win)
Bank Account Number of the Coach
Aadhaar Card
National School Games medal winners by the School Education Department, World / All India University Competition / Championship medal winners by the Higher Education Department / University, Khelo India, Indian Rural Sports Competition / National Women Sports Festival medal winners by the Youth Welfare Department and All India Police Sports Competition / World Police / Fire Games medal winners by Uttarakhand Police Department It will be mandatory to get the sports certificates

scheme_name: Compensation for Loss of Life and Property Caused by Wild Animals in and around Forest Areas: Assistance for Crop Losses Due to Wild Animal Attacks
description: The scheme aims to provide financial assistance to farmers for crop losses caused by wild animals in forest areas and their surrounding regions, thereby mitigating economic losses and supporting farmers’ livelihoods.
benefits:
At present, the following compensation amounts are provided in the event of crop damage caused by wild animal attacks:
Type of Agricultural CropTotal Amount Payable (per Acre)Share of Human Wildlife Conflict Relief Distribution FundSugarcane (Entire Crop)₹25,000/- per acre₹25,000/- per acrePaddy/Wheat/Oilseeds (Entire Crop)₹15,000/- per acre₹15,000/- per acreIn case of damage to all types of crops other than those mentioned above (Entire Crop)₹8,000/- per acre₹8,000/- per acre
eligibility:
1. The applicant must be a resident of Uttarakhand. 
 1. The compensation is applicable for crop damage caused by wild elephants, wild boars, nilgai, kakar, sambar, chital, and monkeys.
application_process:
Mode: Offline. The information must be submitted in writing to the local forest officer within two days of the incident. Following this, the Tehsildar/Patwari and the local forest officer of the area will jointly verify and assess the crop damage. The investigation report will then be forwarded to the concerned Assistant Conservator of Forests/Wildlife Warden through the Range Officer.
The Assistant Conservator of Forests/Wildlife Warden is required to submit the final investigation report to the Divisional Forest Officer/Deputy Director within two months of the incident. Upon receiving the final report, the Divisional Forest Officer/Deputy Director has full authority to approve and disburse the ex-gratia compensation. The Divisional Forest Officer/Deputy Director will also ensure that complete details of the case are communicated to the Chief Wildlife Warden.
Note: The Forest Department has issued a toll-free number – 1800-890-9715. Anyone can use this number to report wildlife incidents, including accidents involving humans or the presence of wildlife in populated areas anywhere in the state.
documents_required:
Identity proof of applicant/farmer
Crop damage assessment report
Bank account details of the applicant
Other supporting documents as required

scheme_name: Compensation for Loss of Life and Property Caused by Wild Animals in and around Forest Areas: Assistance for Loss of Cattle Due to Wild Animal Attacks
description: The scheme aims to provide financial assistance to owners of domestic animals who suffer losses due to attacks by wild animals in forest areas and their surroundings. Under this scheme, a grant ranging from ₹3,000 to ₹40,000 per animal is provided, depending on the species and extent of loss.
benefits:
At present, the following compensation amounts are provided in case of animal loss due to attacks by wild animals:
Type of Animal LossTotal Payable AmountShare of State Disaster Response FundShare of Human Wildlife Conflict Relief Distribution FundMilch Animals- Buffalo / Cow / Camel / Yak / Mithun etc. (Per Animal)₹30,000/-₹30,000/----Agricultural and Transport Animals – Camel, Horse (per Animal)₹40,000/-₹25,000/-₹15,000/-Mule (per Animal)₹40,000/-₹16,000/-₹24,000/-Bull (per Animal)₹25,000/-₹25,000/----Heifer/Donkey/Pony (per Animal)₹16,000/-₹16,000/----Sheep/Goat/Pig (per Animal)₹3,000/-₹3,000/----
eligibility:
1. The applicant must be a permanent resident of Uttarakhand.
 1. The compensation is applicable only for the loss of domestic animals caused by any of the following wild animals:

 - Tiger
 - Leopard
 - Snow Leopard
 - All three species of Bear
 - Hyena
 - Wild Boar
 - Crocodile/Gharial
 - Snake
application_process:
Mode: Offline. In the event of the killing of domestic animals or cattle, the carcass shall be removed from the incident site only after confirmation by the village head or any currently serving public representative. If any poison or pesticide is applied to the carcass, or if it is tampered with in any manner, the ex-gratia payment will not be admissible. The owner must report the killing in writing to the concerned range office within two days of the incident.
Upon confirmation of the killing of domestic animals or cattle by wild animals, firstly by the village head of the area or any currently in-charge public representative, along with the forest guard of the concerned area, 20% of the total payable amount for the incident will be provided to the owner in advance from the available funds. The remaining amount will be disbursed after receipt of the final investigation report.
The certificate of killing of cattle by wild animals will be issued by the concerned Range Officer. Thereafter, the Divisional Forest Officer/Deputy Director shall have full authority to approve and disburse the ex-gratia payment based on the final investigation report submitted by the Assistant Conservator of Forests/Wildlife Warden. In this regard, the Divisional Forest Officer/Deputy Director shall ensure that all relevant information is sent to the Chief Wildlife Warden. The final investigation report will be made available within one month of the incident. If the report does not confirm that the cattle were killed by wild animals, the advance amount already provided to the owner will be recovered as revenue.
Note: The Forest Department has issued a toll-free number (1800-890-9715) for reporting any human-wildlife accidents or the presence of wildlife in populated areas anywhere in the state.
documents_required:
Identity proof of applicant
Proof/Certificate of loss of domestic animal due to wild animal attack
Investigation Report
Other supporting documents as required

scheme_name: Compensation for Loss of Life and Property Caused by Wild Animals in and around Forest Areas: Assistance in case of Death/Injury/Disability due to Wild Animal Attack
description: The scheme aims to provide timely financial assistance and relief to individuals or their dependents in cases of death, injury, or disability caused by attacks from wild animals such as tigers, leopards, elephants, bears, crocodiles, snakes, and other specified species in and around forest
benefits:
*The following compensation amounts are currently given in case of injury/death of a person due to wildlife attack:*
Type of Human InjuryRates payable for ex-gratia amount as per Human Wildlife Conflict Relief Distribution Rules, 2024As per Norms of State Disaster Response Fund (SDRF)Source of Payment : Amount payable from State Disaster Response Fund (SDRF)Source of Payment : Amount payable under Human Wildlife Conflict Relief Distribution Fund Rules 2024Minor Injury1. ₹15,000/- 2. 16,000/-	A deep wound that requires hospitalization: 1.	₹5,400/- per person 2. ₹16,000/- per person₹9,600/- per personSerious Injury₹1,00,000/-A deep wound that requires hospitalization: 1.	₹5,400/- per person 2. ₹16,000/- per person1.	₹94,600/- per person 2. ₹84,000/- per personPartial Disability₹1,00,000/-Loss of any body part (including penis) or eye/eyes: Disability between 40% and 60%: ₹74,000/- per person. ₹74,000/- per person₹26,000/- per personTotal Disability₹3,00,000/- ₹3.00 lakh per person for disability exceeding 60%, subject to certification by a doctor from a Government hospital or dispensary confirming the extent and cause of the disability.₹2,50,000/- per person₹50,000/- per personIn Case of Death of an Adult or a Minor₹6,00,000/- ₹4.00 lakh per person: This includes individuals involved in relief operations or preparedness activities, subject to certification of the cause of death by the competent authority.₹4,00,000/- per person₹2,00,000/- per person*However, for compensation provided for human injury caused by wild animals, it is illegal for family members or any other person to claim the ex-gratia amount if an elderly, medically unfit, disabled, mentally unstable, or minor person is left alone in the forest and is harmed by wild animals.*
eligibility:
1. The applicant must be a resident of Uttarakhand.
1. The applicant or their dependent must have suffered death, injury, or disability due to an attack by a wild animal such as:

 - Tiger
 - Leopard
 - Snow Leopard
 - Wild Elephant
 - All three species of bear
 - Hyena
 - Wild Boar
 - Crocodile / Gharial

application_process:
Mode: Offline. In the event of death, serious injury, or disability caused by a wild animal, 30% of the total compensation amount payable for the incident will be provided to the victim or dependent as an advance. This will be based on the confirmation of the incident by the village head of the affected area, any currently serving public representative, and the forest guard of the concerned area. The advance will be provided within a maximum of 48 hours (excluding public holidays) from the receipt of information regarding the loss of life or property.
The remaining amount will be paid upon receipt of the final investigation report. For the payment of the compensation, the Aadhar card, mobile number, and bank account details of the victim or dependent are required.
In cases where a person is killed, seriously injured, or disabled by a wild animal, a certificate issued by a state government doctor must be submitted to the office of the concerned Divisional Forest Officer (DFO) or Deputy Director. The DFO/Deputy Director will then have full authority to approve or release the ex-gratia payment based on the final investigation report prepared by the concerned Assistant Conservator of Forests or Wildlife Warden. The DFO/Deputy Director will also forward complete details of the case to the Chief Wildlife Warden.
The final investigation report must be submitted within 15 days of the incident. Before making the final payment of the ex-gratia amount, a certificate will be obtained from the Revenue Department regarding the dependents of the deceased. If the final investigation report does not confirm that the victim was killed, seriously injured, or disabled by a wild animal, the advance amount paid to the victim or dependent will be recovered as revenue.
Note: The Forest Department has issued a toll-free number, 1800-890-9715, where any person can report human-wildlife incidents or the presence of wildlife in populated areas anywhere in the state.

benefits:

 1. The project site must be suitable for the construction of artesian wells.
